text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Failures in phone and computer communications in Tallinn cut the government communications lines, stopped stock exchange deals and hit Hansapank.
- Ukrainian Foreign Minister Gennady Udovenko arrived for a two-day visit to discuss bilateral relations and security issues.
- A folk festival in Viljandi began with dances and music by Estonian Swedes.
- 10 members of the Estonian national football team who avoided compulsory military service face two years in prison if their recruitment is not postponed.
- The captain of a Danish Home Guard ship that was visiting Parnu harbour was ordered to pay a fine after 50 litres of oil leaked from the vessel.
- Banks are lowering interest rates amid growing competition and are arriving at the stage where earnings are falling and failing to cover costs, banking experts said.
- Estonian industry grew 12.7 percent in the first half of 1997 while Latvia's and Lithuania's remained on the level of 1996. Estonia's growth was caused by rapid privatisation, analysts say.
